To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a characteristic velocity for flow inside the suction chambers of scroll compressor can be used to predict the Nusselt number and a new heat-transfer correlation for scroll compresser is proposed.

a) the heat transfer coefficient is strongly affected by geometric parameters such as the clearance between the scroll and the suction chamber and the clearance between the compression chamber and the housing, b) the heat transfer correlation for a scroll compressor is strongly dependent on the operating conditions, c) the new correlation proposed in this work is in good agreement with other correlations proposed in the literature and d) the new correlation can be applied for scroll compressors with different geometries and for different operating conditions.
A new heat transfer correlation was proposed for scroll compressors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a better understanding of the fluid mechanics in scroll compressors.
the heat transfer in the suction chamber and the compression chamber of scroll compressors.
the development of a new heat transfer model for scroll compressors and with the proposal of a heat transfer correlation for these machines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heat transfer coefficient is proportional to the square of the characteristic velocity and inversely proportional to the distance between the orifice and the suction or discharge chamber.
the proposed heat transfer correlation for scrolls, based on the proposed characteristic velocity, is the best available in literature.

the proposed correlation is the most accurate one, and it is the one that can be used with more confidence for predicting the heat transfer in the suction chamber and the compression chambers of scroll compressor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed model can predict heat transfer in the suction chamber with good agreement and that the new heat transfer correlation is able to predict the heat transfer in the compression chamber of scroll compressors for a wide range of geometric parameters and operating conditions.
we have developed a model that is able to predict the heat transfer inside the scroll compressor suction and compression chambers.
the heat transfer in the suction chamber of scroll compressors is strongly affected by both the inlet velocity and the inlet temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed heat transfer correlation is valid for a wider range of operating conditions, including low mass flow rates, and that the proposed characteristic velocity can be used for the estimation of the heat transfer coefficient in the suction and the compression chambers of scroll refrigeration systems.
heat transfer inside the scroll chambers is not affected by the scroll geometry, as long as the flow is turbulent.

the heat transfer in scroll compressors can be predicted with an accuracy of 10% with a simple correlation that is a function of the characteristic velocity, the Reynolds number and the heat transfer coefficient of the suction and compression chamber.
